pending_commit.commit_message: Kerberos: Handle bad configuration Handle bad Kerberos configurations. Right now, the daemon crashes since the error happens during context initialization, but printing the error DCHECKs on the context. This CL fixes that and reports a proper error code. The UI should show error 19 (or a proper error saying that the config is bad) and the daemon should not crash. init: Unmount /usr/local only when in dev mode When umounting /usr/local on a user image, unmount will fail. Since cl:919839 we are checking the return status of umount, and since cl:1227868, we will not unmount stateful if we have an error. Therefore all reboots on user image lead to unclean shutdown. Fix the issue by unmounting /usr/local in the opposite function where it has been mounted. BUG=chromium:976135,chromium:835557,chromium:812057 TEST=Check we can unmount properly a test image. Check on a base image, without dev mode: /usr/local is not mounted: Check ext4 "recovery complete" message is not present in dmesg. Change-Id: Ieaae91ef22aba5c81c6938fd67606b7ddb864fb3 Signed-off-by: Gwendal Grignou <gwendal@chromium.org> Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1665988 Legacy-Commit-Queue: Commit Bot <commit-bot@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Mike Frysinger <vapier@chromium.org>

UPSTREAM: BACKPORT: ACPI / button: increment wakeup count only when notified Because acpi_lid_initialize_state() is called on every system resume and it triggers acpi_lid_notify_state() which invokes acpi_pm_wakeup_event() for the lid device, the lid's wakeup count is incremented even if the lid was not the source of the event that woke up the system. That behavior confuses user space deamons using wakeup_count to identify the potential system wakeup source. To avoid the confusion, only trigger acpi_pm_wakeup_event() in the acpi_button_notify() path and don't do that in the acpi_lid_initialize_state() path. BUG=b:65976859 TEST=update_kernel.sh on nocturne and make sure wakeup count for PNP0C0D does not increment, if not the wake source. Signed-off-by: Ravi Chandra Sadineni <ravisadineni@chromium.org> Signed-off-by: Rafael J. CHROMIUM: drm/i915: Add missing access checks in i915_gem_execbuffer2_ioctl CVE-2018-20669: An issue where a provided address with access_ok() is not checked was discovered in i915_gem_execbuffer2_ioctl in drivers/gpu/drm/i915/i915_gem_execbuffer.c in the Linux kernel through 4.19.13. A local attacker can craft a malicious IOCTL function call to overwrite arbitrary kernel memory, resulting in a Denial of Service or privilege escalation. The problem is fixed upstream with commit 594cc251fdd0 ("make 'user_access_begin()' do 'access_ok()'"), which merges access_ok into user_access_begin() system-wide. Since this would be difficult to backport, add the missing calls to access_ok() locally. BUG=chromium:976652 TEST=Run i915 graphics tests Change-Id: I6868f0f2f59c907d0c2191621fd714cc3c8d7d5a Signed-off-by: Guenter Roeck <groeck@chromium.org> Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1668054 Legacy-Commit-Queue: Commit Bot <commit-bot@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Stéphane Marchesin <marcheu@chromium.org>
